citations.claim: the /01/ form with an https domain and 14-digit GTIN is conformant
citations.evidence: DL URI Syntax 1.7.0 §4 (ABNF), §4.11 "Constructing the GS1 Digital Link URI": scheme="http" / "https" / "HTTP" / "HTTPS". otherClaims.claim: the QR must use /01/ in place of /gtin/
some scanners may still resolve /gtin/, but it is non-conformant

answers.notes: Plus one check_gtin call. Self-corrected: call 3 added https://, call 4 set useConvenienceAlphas; the answer relies on call 4 (and on call 3 for the /01/ pass). Says its first call's domain failure was its own input error. Reports the advisory severity faithfully. Caveats that size/height/quiet-zone figures are engine defaults; names WHAT-IS-NOT-CHECKED and that a clean result is not compliance. The two transcription entries are on superseded calls and did not reach the final verdict. The schema field is named `domain` with no description; the engine requires an origin with scheme (rules/gs1/digitalLink.ts tests /^https?:\/\//) and returns GS1_DIGITAL_LINK_INVALID before evaluating useConvenienceAlphas, so the dropped scheme alone also suppresses the planted finding. All five answers in this case that sent a Digital Link sent a bare host name first - an interface defect worth recording, though the engine's verdict on the string it got (a URI with no http/https scheme is non-conformant, DL §4.11) is correct.

citations.claim: 036000291452 has a valid check digit
citations.evidence: GenSpecs 26.0 p.544 (rendered and read) §7.9.1 "Standard check digit calculations for GS1 data structures": "This algorithm is identical for all fixed length numeric GS1 data structures (including GDTI, GLN, GRAI, etc.) that require a check digit." Table 7-8: GTIN-12 positions N1..N12, multipliers x3,x1,...; "Subtract sum from nearest equal or higher multiple of ten = check digit".
